body.statement:
Suppose \(n\to\infty\), \(c_-\le m/n\le c_+\), and \(r,\mu,K,q\) are fixed, and define
\[
 d_{nm}=\sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}\left[1\wedge
 \frac B{\lambda_{nm}}\left\{
 q^{-1}\sqrt{(n\vee m)\log(e(n+m))}+q^{-3}\log(en)
 \right\}\right].
\]
If \(b_{nm}=o(1)\), then the truncations in both \(b_{nm}\) and \(d_{nm}\) are eventually inactive and
\[
 b_{nm}\asymp\frac{B\sqrt{n\log(en)}}{\lambda_{nm}},
 \qquad
 d_{nm}\asymp\sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}\,b_{nm}.
\]
In particular \(d_{nm}/b_{nm}\asymp\sqrt n\to\infty\), so \(d_{nm}=O(b_{nm})\) is not a nonempty fixed-complexity subregime under \(b_{nm}=o(1)\).
body.proof_tex:
Write
\[
 s_{nm}=\sqrt{n^{-1}+nm^{-2}}
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 t_{nm}=\frac{B\sqrt{nm}}{\lambda_{nm}}\sqrt{\log(en)}\,
 K r^{3/2}\mu q^{-1/2}s_{nm}.
\]
By \(\mathrm{ass:aspect\mbox{-}ratio}\),
\[
 s_{nm}
 =n^{-1/2}\sqrt{1+(n/m)^2}
 \asymp n^{-1/2}
\]
and
\[
 \sqrt{nm}\,s_{nm}
 =\sqrt{m+n^2/m}
 \asymp\sqrt n.
\]
All implicit constants in these comparisons depend only on \(c_-\) and \(c_+\).  Since \(r,\mu,K,q\) are fixed and positive, \(\mathrm{def:geometric\mbox{-}rate}\) and \(\mathrm{def:frontier\mbox{-}rate}\) give
\[
 b_{nm}=1\wedge t_{nm},
 \qquad
 t_{nm}\asymp
 \frac{B\sqrt{n\log(en)}}{\lambda_{nm}}.
\]
The hypothesis \(b_{nm}=o(1)\) implies \(b_{nm}<1\) eventually.  For such indices, \(1\wedge t_{nm}<1\) forces \(t_{nm}<1\), so \(b_{nm}=t_{nm}\).  Consequently the truncation in \(b_{nm}\) is eventually inactive and
\[
 b_{nm}\asymp
 \frac{B\sqrt{n\log(en)}}{\lambda_{nm}}.
\]

For the second radius, put
\[
 x_{nm}=\frac B{\lambda_{nm}}
 \left\{
 q^{-1}\sqrt{(n\vee m)\log(e(n+m))}
 +q^{-3}\log(en)
 \right\}.
\]
The aspect-ratio bounds imply \(n\vee m\asymp n\) and
\(\log(e(n+m))\asymp\log(en)\).  Moreover,
\[
 \frac{\log(en)}{\sqrt{n\log(en)}}
 =\sqrt{\frac{\log(en)}n}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Because \(q\) is fixed and positive, it follows that
\[
 x_{nm}\asymp
 \frac{B\sqrt{n\log(en)}}{\lambda_{nm}}
 \asymp b_{nm}=o(1).
\]
Thus \(x_{nm}<1\) eventually, so the truncation in the definition of \(d_{nm}\) is also inactive.  Hence
\[
 d_{nm}
 =\sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}\,x_{nm}
 \asymp
 \sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}\,b_{nm}.
\]
The quantities \(B,\lambda_{nm},q,K,r,\mu,n,m\) are positive, so \(b_{nm}>0\) and division is legitimate.  Since \(r\) and \(\mu\) are fixed,
\[
 \frac{d_{nm}}{b_{nm}}\asymp\sqrt n\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Therefore no dimension path satisfying the stated fixed-complexity hypotheses and \(b_{nm}=o(1)\) can also satisfy \(d_{nm}=O(b_{nm})\).
body.justification: Nonemptiness and bounded outcomes expose the scale floor that governs whether the stated uniform radii can shrink.
body.gap: At fixed complexity, \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) and \(d_{nm}\) are at least order \(\sqrt{\log n}\), so neither is a shrinking uniform resolution.
body.consumer: Blind-diagnostic and minimax claims are interpreted only at resolutions compatible with the bounded-outcome class.
